heading: INT. MOBILE MRI TRAILER - PARKED BEHIND RURAL CLINIC - MORNING

units.text: INT. MOBILE MRI TRAILER - PARKED BEHIND RURAL CLINIC - MORNING
A white box on wheels with a humming magnet at its heart.
A glass partition.
On the other side, a patient lies on a sliding table with his head in a cage.
DR. SABINA ROTHENBERG, forties, radiologist, sits at the console, tapping the mouse.
Beside her, TECHNOLOGIST FELIX AGYEMAN, thirties, adjusts a dial.
On the table, ARMANDO KESSLER, sixty, a farmer, looks at the ceiling.
Mr. Kessler, this is the last sequence. Just breathe normally.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: Doc, you've said that three times.
units.name: ARMANDO

units.text: And I mean it more each time.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: Felix smiles briefly.
The magnet knocks in a steady rhythm.
Motion's good. He's a model patient.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: He's lying very still.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: That's what I said.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Felix, when did he last eat?
units.name: SABINA

units.text: Six, he said. He drove forty miles.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Mm.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: The images build on the monitor, slice by slice.
Sabina leans closer.
Her smile slackens.
Everything okay?
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Yes.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: You went quiet.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: I'm reading.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: The magnet knocks.
Felix watches her for a long moment, and then looks at the screen.
Is that --
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Don't.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: It's bilateral.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: I said don't.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: Sabina.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Not until he's out of the machine.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: Felix slowly takes his hand off the dial.
Everything all right in there? You two have gone awful quiet.
units.name: ARMANDO

units.text: Sabina presses the button.
Everything's fine, Mr. Kessler. A few more minutes.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: She releases it and sits very still, and Felix, without a word, reaches over and turns the monitor away from the glass.
The magnet knocks.
And knocks.
